name: Daily Sacrifice The
overview: The daily sacrifice, as outlined in Leviticus and Numbers, was a continual burnt offering ordained at Mount Sinai, involving a lamb offered morning and evening with accompanying meat and drink offerings. The fire on the altar was to remain perpetually burning, symbolizing a sweet savour and constant dedication to the Lord. Priests were to carefully manage the ashes and maintain the fire, ensuring the sacrifice was slowly and entirely consumed, reflecting the sacred and perpetual nature of this ordinance.
